steps.body: What is cos(arcsin(3/5))? Name the hidden angle: θ = arcsin(3/5) means **sin θ = 3/5 with θ in the branch**. Draw the helper right triangle — opposite 3, hypotenuse 5 — and the missing leg is 4 (recall 3-4-5). So cos θ = **4/5**, no calculator, exactly.

predict.prompt: Opposite is 3, hypotenuse is 5. As you slide the adjacent leg longer, what happens to the hypotenuse reading?

options.label: It grows too, until one exact length makes it read 5
It stays 5 no matter what — hypotenuse is fixed by the angle alone
It shrinks, since a longer adjacent leaves less for the hypotenuse

predict.reveal: The hypotenuse is the far side of a triangle whose other two legs you are setting — stretch either leg and it has to grow to reach across. Only ONE adjacent length makes it land on exactly 5 with opposite held at 3.

widget.prompt: The angle's vertex sits at the origin. Opposite is fixed at 3. Drag the point until the hypotenuse reads exactly 5 — its x-coordinate is the adjacent leg.
widget.successFeedback: √(4² + 3²) = √25 = 5 — the classic 3-4-5 triple. The adjacent leg is 4, and you found it by watching the hypotenuse arrive at 5, not by recalling a formula.
widget.wrongPointFeedback: Not yet — read the number under the square root. If it shows 34, you added 5² to 3² instead of using 5 as the HYPOTENUSE (the longest side, opposite the right angle) and solving for the shorter leg: adjacent² = 5² − 3², not 5² + 3². If it shows 2, that subtracted the legs directly (5 − 3) instead of subtracting their SQUARES and rooting the result.

explanationVariants: cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 4/5 = 0.8 — and the identity route agrees: cos θ = √(1 − (3/5)²) = 4/5.
The branch guarantees θ is Quadrant I here (positive input), so cosine is positive: +0.8.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.6 = 3/5 is the SINE. Cosine reads the adjacent leg: 4/5 = 0.8.
3/4 mixes the two legs. Cosine is adjacent over HYPOTENUSE: 4/5.

steps.body: The identity route (recall sin²θ + cos²θ = 1) gives the same answer: cos θ = ±√(1 − v²), and the **branch chooses the sign** — arcsin's outputs in [−π/2, π/2] always have cos θ ≥ 0, so cos(arcsin v) = **+√(1 − v²)** for every valid v, even negative ones.

explanationVariants: cos(arcsin(−3/5)) = +√(1 − 9/25) = 4/5: the branch angle −θ has POSITIVE cosine (cosine is even).
arcsin(−3/5) lands at a negative branch angle, and every branch angle has non-negative cosine: +0.8.

options.label: +4/5 — branch angles always have cos ≥ 0
options.feedback: Right — arcsin(−3/5) = −θ sits in [−π/2, 0), where cosine is still positive: 4/5.
Cosine is EVEN: cos(−θ) = cos(θ) = 4/5. Negative sines don't make negative cosines on this branch.
−3/5 is the sine (the input). The cosine of the hidden angle is √(1 − 9/25) = +4/5.

explanationVariants: θ = arccos(5/13): adjacent 5, hypotenuse 13 → opposite 12 (5-12-13); tan θ = 12/5 = 2.4.
Identity route: sin θ = √(1 − 25/169) = 12/13, and tan = sin/cos = (12/13)/(5/13) = 12/5.

commonErrors.feedback: 5/12 inverts the ratio. Tangent is OPPOSITE over adjacent: 12/5 = 2.4.
12/13 is the SINE. Divide by the cosine 5/13: tan = 12/5 = 2.4.
13/5 uses the hypotenuse. Tangent never does: 12/5 = 2.4.

explanationVariants: θ = arctan(3/4): opposite 3, adjacent 4 → hypotenuse 5. sin θ = 3/5 = 0.6; the branch angle for a positive tangent is Quadrant I, so the sign is +.

commonErrors.feedback: 0.75 = 3/4 is the TANGENT (the input). Sine needs the hypotenuse 5: 3/5 = 0.6.
0.8 = 4/5 is the COSINE of this angle. Sine takes the opposite leg: 3/5 = 0.6.

steps.body: Name the angle, draw the triangle.
takeaways: Set θ = the inner inverse; its definition labels two triangle sides.
Pythagoras supplies the third; read off the outer function.
Branch ranges fix the sign: cos(arcsin v) = +√(1 − v²) always.
steps.teaser: Finale: solving trig equations — inverse gives ONE answer, the circle gives them all.

concept.body: For outer(inner-inverse(v)): let θ be the inner angle, draw its right triangle from the ratio v, complete with Pythagoras, then evaluate the outer ratio — sign from the branch.

explanationVariants: θ = arccos(0.6): adjacent 3, hypotenuse 5, opposite 4 → sin θ = 4/5 = 0.8.
Identity: sin θ = √(1 − 0.36) = 0.8, positive on [0, π].

commonErrors.feedback: 0.6 is the cosine you started with. The sine is √(1 − 0.36) = 0.8.
